discovery: Discovery of collective motion as a nonequilibrium phase transition and the hydrodynamic theory of flocking (active matter)

nominees.name: Yuhai Tu
nominees.affiliation: IBM T. J. Watson Research Center, USA

subfield: Statistical physics / nonequilibrium and active matter
motivation: A flock of birds is a very simple problem to state and very hard to understand. In 1995 Vicsek and collaborators showed with a minimal model of self-propelled particles that aligning agents undergo a genuine phase transition to collective order, a surprising result since in equilibrium such long-range order in two dimensions is forbidden by the Mermin-Wagner theorem. Toner and Tu then built the hydrodynamic field theory of flocks, using the renormalization group to explain how motion itself stabilizes true long-range order, with anomalous giant number fluctuations and nontrivial scaling. Together these works founded the physics of active matter, a new chapter of statistical mechanics far from equilibrium, now confirmed in bacterial suspensions, motile colloids, cytoskeletal extracts and field observations of starling flocks. The concepts have spread across biology, soft matter and robotics: a new framework revealing hidden order in apparent disorder, and a beautiful example of fundamental science opening unexpected avenues.
